main_text.head: Prioris exempla.
main_text.p: 7. Qui à senis aureis decem ursa-torum lucrum quærit, quanti uendet pondo mercis, 20 ursatis emptum?

p.i: Quoniam hic diuersi nominis pecunia datur, primum sex aureos antecedete multiplicatione in ursatos redigo, 15 ursatos monetæ Basilienfis pro aureo cōputando, fa-ctus erit 90. Huic si lucrum addidero, totus ursat. scilicet 100, erit medius proportionis terminus, in hunc modum:

main_text.p: 8. Lanius famulu 216 aureis in-structum ad mercatu misit, mandans, ut æquali numero tot capita boum, uitulorum, ueruecum atq; porcorum emat, quot ea pecunia suppeditare po test. Ambigitur de singularum bestia-rum numero.

p.i: Fingamus primum pretia: bouis, aureorum unde-cim, uituli duorum, ueruecis unius cum ursatis 5, porci trium cum ursatis 10. Hic igitur duplici multiplica-tione cum additione opus erit, ad principem proportio-nem informandam. Oportet enim 216 aureos per 15 (tot enim ursatis uulgus Germanorum aureum taxat) in 3240 ursatos resoluere, similiterq; singularū bestia-rum

page.notes: The marginal figure at the right (a small fraction and arithmetic diagram beside the lines of the text) is not transcribed as text. The left-edge fragments belong to the facing page. The catchword is not printed. Some words in the mathematical lines (for example "tum è", "ergo") are read with uncertainty; the bold ending "rum" at the foot is a catchword-like continuation of "bestiarum" and is shown as printed.
